proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium phosphate. It is chemically compatible with both the sulfide electrolyte and the oxide cathode, and it is usually reported as a stable interfacial buffer that suppresses cathode-sulfide reactions at about 4 V. This is a single-evaluation pick, so the choice of polymorph is a guess.

Li3AlF6 is a wide-gap, insulating lithium fluoride whose fluoride anions resist oxidation near 4 V. Al3+ is hard to reduce, so it should be less prone to reduction by Li6PS5Cl than the Ti or Nb oxides, and it may avoid the P-S-O side reactions that gave Li3PO4 a large penalty. Its contact with LiCoO2 and the sulfide is untested.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) gave a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/atom, far above the 0.05 limit, because it reacts with the sulfide to form P2O5 and SCl4 products. A different, fluoride-based family is needed to lower the penalty.
